BRCA1 and 2 mutations occur in approximately 10% of patients with breast cancer.

PARP inhibitors are a new class of targeted therapy that are effective in treating breast cancer associated with BRCA mutation, particularly when used in combination with platinum agents and/or chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie resistance to chemotherapy and endocrine therapy and the development of strategies to overcome these mechanisms.
the treatment of breast cancers associated with germline and somatic mutations of DNA damage repair genes.
the treatment and prevention of breast cancer in patients with a BRCA mutation and the role of DDR in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PARP inhibitors have a role in the treatment of BRCA positive metastatic breast cancer.
PARP inhibitors have a role to play in BRCA1 and 2 associated metastatic breast cancer.
the best treatment for breast cancers with BRCA mutation would be a combination of PARP inhibitor and platinum based chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PARP inhibitors are effective for patients with BRCA mutated metastatic breast cancers.
the data for PARP inhibition in BRCA1 and/or 2 mutated breast cancer is robust and that these agents should be considered as part of the standard of care for patients with metastatic disease.
PARP inhibitors are active in the BRCA mutated setting and that there are some differences between the agents that have been tested in the clinical setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BRCA status of the tumour is important in the selection of the optimal therapy for the patient.

PARP inhibition is a new treatment modality that has been proven effective in patients with germline BRCA mutations and that this treatment modality has been proven to have activity in the metastatic setting, in the adjuvant setting and in the neoadjuvant setting.
PARP inhibition is a promising new treatment for metastatic HER2 negative, HR positive breast cancer, and should be considered as a treatment option.
